  5C)             In 1796, Edward Jenner, an English physician noticed that dairy workers who had  
  caught relatively mild disease cowpox from cows seemed to be immune to smallpox. He  
  found that rubbing pus from cowpox sores into scratches in the skin prevented people  
  from coming down with smallpox later. Almost a century later, Louis Pasteur found a  
  safer way to prepare vaccines. He discovered how to attenuate (kill them so that they  
  will infect, but no disease is caused) microorganisms until they could no longer cause  
  disease. Smallpox was not only the first disease to be prevented by vaccination but also  
  the first disease to be officially eradicated by human efforts.                          (4)  
  i) How does vaccination protect the body from getting disease?  
  ii) Is it safe to use attenuated microorganisms as vaccines?  
  iii) Explain why rubbing pus from cowpox sores into scratches in the skin prevented  
  people from getting smallpox.  
  iv) Give the reason why several diseases such as common cold, chicken pox, corona etc  
  have remained ineffective or partially effective against vaccines.  
  (1+1+1+1 = 4 marks)
